title: Fit and proper vs competence: what is the difference?
description: Competence is the ability to do the job; fit and proper is a wider suitability test for key roles that adds honesty, integrity and judgment to competence.
shortAnswer: Competence is the ability to apply knowledge and skills to achieve intended results, as ISO 9000 defines it, and applies to anyone whose work matters. Fit and proper is a regulatory suitability test for people in key roles, such as directors, senior managers and control function heads in financial institutions. It includes competence but adds character: honesty, integrity, diligence and sound judgment, assessed before appointment and reassessed regularly.
keyTakeaways: Competence is one part of fitness and propriety: a person can be highly competent and still fail a fit and proper assessment on integrity grounds.
Fit and proper tests apply to defined key roles; competence requirements usually apply to every person whose work affects quality, safety or compliance.
Australia's APRA lists the criteria in SPS 520: competence, character, diligence, experience, honesty, integrity and judgment, plus education or technical qualifications, knowledge and skills.
In the EU, the joint EBA and ESMA suitability guidelines govern management body members, while MiFID II separately requires knowledge and competence for staff who advise or inform clients.
Training evidence supports competence directly; for fit and proper it supports only the knowledge element, alongside background checks, references and declarations.

sections.heading: What is the core difference between fit and proper and competence?

blocks.text: The core difference is scope. Competence asks whether a person can do the work. Fit and proper asks whether a person should be trusted with a key role, and answers it by combining competence with character and reputation. Training can build competence; it cannot make someone proper.

ISO 9000:2015, quoted in [ISO auditing practices guidance](https://committee.iso.org/files/live/sites/tc176/files/PDF%20APG%20New%20Disclaimer%2012-2023/ISO-TC%20176-TF_APG-Competence.pdf), defines competence as the "ability to apply knowledge and skills to achieve intended results". Management system standards such as ISO 9001 require organizations to determine the competence needed for work affecting performance and to ensure people are competent on the basis of education, training or experience. See [competence vs competency](/compare/competence-vs-competency) for the related distinction.

Fit and proper is a prudential concept. The Australian Prudential Regulation Authority (APRA) standard [SPS 520 Fit and Proper](https://www.apra.gov.au/standards/sps-520) requires a registrable superannuation entity licensee to assess each responsible person before appointment and annually, against criteria including competence, character, diligence, experience, honesty, integrity and judgment, and appropriate education or technical qualifications, knowledge and skills. Detail is on [APRA SPS 510 and SPS 520](/regulations/apra-superannuation-sps-510-fit-and-proper-training).

sections.heading: How do major regimes treat the two concepts?

blocks.text: Most financial regimes run both tests side by side: a fit and proper test for a small group of key people, and a competence standard for a wider population of staff. The examples below show the pattern.

items: **Australia:** SPS 520 requires competencies to be documented for each responsible person position and assessment before appointment and annually. A [June 2026 APRA consultation](https://www.apra.gov.au/governance-review-consultation-paper) proposes narrowing the population of responsible persons and keeping the Financial Accountability Regime as the main accountability mechanism; see [Financial Accountability Regime training](/regulations/financial-accountability-regime-training).

**European Union, management bodies:** the [joint EBA and ESMA suitability guidelines](https://www.eba.europa.eu/sites/default/files/document_library/Publications/Guidelines/2021/EBA-GL-2021-06%20Joint%20GLs%20on%20the%20assessment%20of%20suitability%20%28fit%26propoer%29/1022127/Final%20report%20on%20joint%20EBA%20and%20ESMA%20GL%20on%20the%20assessment%20of%20suitability.pdf) (EBA/GL/2021/06) cover the suitability of management body members and key function holders, and require newly appointed members to receive key information within one month and complete induction within six months. Article 91(9) of the [Capital Requirements Directive](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32013L0036) requires institutions to devote adequate human and financial resources to induction and training of management body members.

**European Union, client facing staff:** [MiFID II Article 25(1)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32014L0065) requires investment firms to ensure and demonstrate that staff giving investment advice or information have the necessary knowledge and competence. [ESMA guidelines](https://www.esma.europa.eu/sites/default/files/library/esma71-1154262120-153_guidelines_for_the_assessment_of_knowledge_and_competence_corrigendum.pdf) set an appropriate qualification, at least six months of appropriate experience and an annual review. This is a competence test, not a fit and proper test; see [MiFID II knowledge and competence](/regulations/mifid-ii-knowledge-and-competence-requirements).

**UAE, DIFC:** the Dubai Financial Services Authority requires a firm to be satisfied that an authorized individual is fit and proper before applying ([GEN 7.6.1](https://dfsaen.thomsonreuters.com/rulebook/gen-761-0)), assessed under GEN App7, which lists competence and capability among the factors ([GEN A7.1.1](https://dfsaen.thomsonreuters.com/rulebook/gen-a711)). [GEN 7.7.1](https://dfsaen.thomsonreuters.com/rulebook/gen-771) requires at least annual review of fitness, competence and currency of knowledge.

**AML staff screening:** EU AMLR Article 13 requires obliged entities to assess relevant staff's skills, knowledge and expertise and their good repute, honesty and integrity, a fit and proper style test applied below board level.

blocks.title: Practical consequence
blocks.text: Keep two records per key person: a suitability file covering character, reputation and declarations, and a competence file covering knowledge, skills, training and assessment. The competence file is updated far more often and is the one learning teams own.
Fit and proper applies when a regulator names the role; competence applies to almost every role in a regulated organization. Start from the regulator's list of key roles and build outward.

items: **Board members, senior executives and control function heads in banks, insurers, superannuation and investment firms:** both. Assess fitness and propriety at appointment and periodically, and maintain a competence and induction record.

**Client facing advisers and sales staff:** competence standards such as MiFID II or Australia's adviser professional standards; see [financial services competence requirements by country](/compare/financial-services-competence-requirements-by-country).
**Operational staff in any regulated sector:** competence under the relevant standard or law, evidenced through a [competency framework](/glossary/competency-framework) and assessment.
**AML relevant staff in the EU from July 10, 2027:** AMLR Article 13 screening of skills and integrity, plus training under Article 12; see [AML vs KYC](/compare/aml-vs-kyc).

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry defines the competencies each key role requires, links them to the rule that demands them, and attaches assessment points and evidence. That gives fit and proper reviewers a current, sourced competence record to draw on, while character and reputation checks stay in the suitability process where they belong.

faqs.q: Can someone be competent but not fit and proper?
faqs.a: Yes. Fit and proper criteria include honesty, integrity and character as well as competence. A highly qualified and experienced person can fail the test because of dishonest conduct, adverse findings by a court or regulator, or undisclosed conflicts. Training does not address those concerns.

faqs.q: How often must fit and proper assessments be repeated?
faqs.a: It depends on the regime. APRA's SPS 520 requires assessment before appointment and annually. The DFSA's GEN 7.7.1 requires at least annual review of authorized individuals' fitness, competence and currency of knowledge. Most regimes also require reassessment when new information arises.

faqs.q: Is MiFID II knowledge and competence a fit and proper test?
faqs.a: No. MiFID II Article 25(1) and the ESMA guidelines set knowledge and competence requirements for staff who give investment advice or information. They focus on qualifications, experience and annual review. Suitability of management body members is covered separately by the joint EBA and ESMA guidelines.

faqs.q: Does training count toward a fit and proper assessment?
faqs.a: It supports the competence element. Training and assessment records help show that a person has the knowledge and skills for the role and keeps them current. Regulators also expect induction for new board members, which the EBA and ESMA guidelines time at one and six months.
